$comment: TF-C114 (D-OPT-SIMPLIFYCFG-EMPTY-SELF-LOOP-REDIRECT-CYCLE): the RUN witness for an all-trampoline CFG cycle. SimplifyCfg jump-threads blocks whose only instruction is a `Br`; when a cycle is made ENTIRELY of such blocks the redirect map becomes B1->B2->...->Bk->B1 and the transitive walk aborted the compiler (`resolveTransitive exceeded chain length`, rc=127, NO binary) on all three shipped targets at --config=release only. main.c carries four cycle lengths — k=2 via `for(;;){}`, k=2 via a two-label goto ring (proving the shape is not about the `for` spelling), k=3, and k=1 (`goto` to its own label, the ONE length a bespoke self-target check already covered before the fix, kept as a regression pin on that check's deletion). Every loop is guarded by `argc > <big>` so it is PRESENT in the MIR the pass processes but never ENTERED at runtime (argc==1 under the harness); `argc` is a runtime value so ConstFold cannot fold the guard away and make the example vacuous — an entered infinite loop could never exit and would hang the runner. The `release` arm (shippedPipeline, zero-drift) is the load-bearing one: the defect is RELEASE-ONLY, so the baseline arm was green throughout and could never have caught it. RED-on-disable: revert breakJumpThreadCycles in src/opt/passes/simplify_cfg.cpp -> the release arm's compile aborts rc=127 with no binary. exitCode 42.
